name: Beartown Mountain
generated_description:
Beartown Mountain is a 4,688-foot summit in Virginia. The Beartown Mountain Trail covers 5.7 miles with about 564 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

The grade is back-loaded: the first half of the route climbs gently, and most of the elevation gain comes in the second half. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 2.83, gaining roughly 1,400 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 3,419 feet, the route tops out near 3,983 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 36.8698, -81.9628 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 95 miles north of Asheville, North Carolina. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Late May through October is the main season. Snow and ice linger into spring and return early in fall at this latitude and elevation; in winter this becomes a different, more serious undertaking requiring traction devices and warm layers.

Know Before You Go

Most hikers should budget about 2.0 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Redrock Mountain, Flattop Mountain and Double Top — each has its own guide on this site.
